'''Consumer Cellular, Inc.''' is an American [[postpaid mobile phone|postpaid]] [[mobile virtual network operator]] founded by John Marick and Greg Pryor in Portland, Oregon, in October 1995.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/tech/columnist/baig/2017/07/03/cell-phone-plans-seniors-offer-more-service-lighter-data/103037490/|title=Cellphone plans for seniors offer more service, lighter data|website=USA TODAY}}</ref> The company offers cellphones, no-contract cellphone plans, and accessories with a focus on users over age 50. Including its corporate headquarters in [[Scottsdale, Arizona]], Consumer Cellular is completely U.S. based, employing more than 3,100 people in Arizona, Oregon, Oklahoma, Kentucky and Texas.<ref name=factsheet>[https://www.consumercellular.com/content/dam/consumercellularincprogram/web/pages/press/PR%20Fact%20Sheet%202024.pdf Consumer Cellular Fact Sheet], www.consumercellular.com</ref>

Consumer Cellular provides wireless service using network capacity from [[AT&T]] and [[T-Mobile US|T-Mobile]], with only AT&T being used for new activations as of 2024,<ref name="ConsumerCellularInc">{{cite web | title=Determining which provider | author=ConsumerCellularInc | date=14 July 2024 | publisher=Reddit | url=https://www.reddit.com/r/consumercellular/comments/1e1ks2q/comment/ld6fv6q | accessdate=2024-11-04}}</ref> and also resells AT&T wholesale wireless services to other virtual operators. The company was included on the Inc 5000 list as one of America's fastest growing companies every year between 2009 and 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inc.com/profile/consumer-cellular|title=Consumer Cellular is on the Private Titans|website=Inc.com}}</ref> {{As of| August 2020}}, when it put itself up for sale, the company had close to 4&nbsp;million subscribers.<ref>{{Cite web|work=[[Light Reading]]|first=Mike|last=Dano|url=https://www.lightreading.com/services/consumer-cellular-fielding-interest-from-buyers---sources/d/d-id/763109?|title = Consumer Cellular fielding interest from buyers - sources|date=August 11, 2020|access-date=November 15, 2023}}</ref> In October 2020, Chicago private equity company [[GTCR]] purchased Consumer Cellular for about $2.3 billion.<ref>{{Citation|work=[[Light Reading]]|first=Mike|last=Dano|title=Consumer Cellular sold to private equity firm for around $2.3B|url=https://www.lightreading.com/oss-bss-cx/consumer-cellular-sold-to-private-equity-firm-for-around-2-3b|date=October 27, 2020|access-date=November 15, 2023}}</ref>

==History==
John Marick and Greg Pryor founded Consumer Cellular in 1995 with a goal of providing low-cost service to casual mobile users of all ages.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.entrepreneur.com/article/227569|title=Catering to Boomers, a Cell Phone Company Takes Off|first=Sarah|last=Max|date=30 July 2013|website=Entrepreneur}}</ref> In 2008, Consumer Cellular became a preferred provider for [[AARP]] members, becoming the first cellphone company to market extensively to the over-50 demographic.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.opb.org/news/article/small-portland-cellular-provider-teams-aarp/|title=Small Portland Cellular Provider Teams Up With AARP|first=Pete|last=Springer|website=www.opb.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=William |title=Efficient Communication Solutions for Seniors: Consumer Cellular in Focus |url=https://www.pressconnects.com/story/special/contributor-content/2025/10/27/efficient-communication-solutions-for-seniors-consumer-cellular-in-focus/86929745007/ |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=Press & Sun-Bulletin |language=en-US}}</ref>

The company's first retail presence was established in 2011 with a partnership with [[Sears]] stores. In 2014, Consumer Cellular was introduced in [[Target Corporation|Target]] stores,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/silicon-forest/2014/03/consumer_cellular_approaching_1.html|title=Consumer Cellular, approaching a half-billion dollars in annual sales, gets tryout with Target|first=Mike|last=Rogoway |date=30 March 2014|website=oregonlive.com}}</ref> and in 2018 became available at select U.S. [[Best Buy]] stores.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bestmvno.com/consumer-cellular/consumer-cellular-now-available-at-best-buy-on-track-for-3-million-subscribers/|title=Consumer Cellular Now Available At Best Buy, On Track For 3 Million Subscribers|date=10 August 2018|publisher=}}</ref> In 2013, the company introduced a smartphone financing program called EasyPay that is available to consumers purchasing smartphones that cost $200 and up.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.phonescoop.com/articles/article.php?a=12705|title=Consumer Cellular Intros EasyPay Financing Program|website=Phone Scoop}}</ref> That same year, the company partnered with [[SquareTrade]] to begin providing cellphone protection plans.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.telecompaper.com/news/consumer-cellular-adds-squaretrade-protection-plans--964821 |title=Consumer Cellular adds SquareTrade protection plans |website=www.telecompaper.com}}</ref> In May 2018, Consumer Cellular announced an investment in GrandPad<ref name="biz">{{cite news |last=Spencer |first=Malia |date=May 21, 2018 |title=Consumer Cellular invests in senior-aimed tablet startup |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/portland/news/2018/05/21/consumer-cellular-invests-in-senior-focused-tablet.html |access-date=May 13, 2020 |newspaper=Portland Business Journal}}</ref> and also became a distributor of the GrandPad tablet in the United States.<ref name="seattle">{{cite news |last=Kharif |first=Olga |date=May 13, 2018 |title=An iPad for 80-year-olds: Senior-citizen carrier Consumer Cellular bets on tablets |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/business/an-ipad-for-80-year-olds-senior-citizen-carrier-consumer-cellular-bets-on-tablets/ |access-date=May 13, 2020 |newspaper=The Seattle Times}}</ref>

In February 2013, in celebration of its one millionth customer, Consumer Cellular donated $100,000 to each of five non-profit partners, and $500,000 to its employees, for a total of $1&nbsp;million. To celebrate its 20th anniversary and its milestone of 2&nbsp;million customers, it donated $2&nbsp;million to the Knight Cancer Challenge on behalf of their customers in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bizjournals.com/portland/blog/health-care-inc/2015/06/portland-company-gives-2m-to-knight-cancer.html|title=Portland company gives $2M to Knight Cancer Challenge|website=Portland Business Journal}}</ref> After reaching 2.5&nbsp;million customers in the summer of 2017, it donated 2.5&nbsp;million meals via [[Feeding America]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://1859oregonmagazine.com/think-oregon/business/consumer-cellular-gives-back-to-fight-hunger/|title=Consumer Cellular Gives Back to Fight Hunger|date=24 May 2017|publisher=}}</ref> and to mark the addition of its 3&nbsp;millionth customer in October 2018, the company donated $500,000 to each of three charities selected by its employees.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.einnews.com/pr_news/464481279/consumer-cellular-commemorates-three-millionth-customer-by-gifting-three-million-dollars |title=Consumer Cellular Commemorates Three Millionth Customer by Gifting Three Million Dollars |publisher=EIN News |date=2018-10-09 |accessdate=2019-04-03}}</ref> 

In August 2019, the company celebrated its 3.5 millionth customer by donating $350,000 to the American Red Cross through the Disaster Responder Program.<ref>[https://www.redcross.org/about-us/news-and-events/press-release/2019/consumer-cellular-celebrates-3-5-millionth-customer-by-gifting-350000-to-the-american-red-cross.html Consumer Cellular Celebrates 3.5 Millionth Customer by Gifting $350,000 to the American Red Cross]</ref> In the fall of 2020, to honor its 25th anniversary, Consumer Cellular donated $2.5&nbsp;million to [[Toys for Tots]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-10-15 |title=Consumer Cellular gives $2.5M to Toys for Tots |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/portland/news/2020/10/15/consumer-cellular-gives-2-5m-to-toys-for-tots.html |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=Portland Business Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> In October 2020, upon the decision of Marick and Pryor to retire, Ed Evans was installed as CEO, replacing Marick.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/silicon-forest/2020/10/consumer-cellular-one-of-oregons-biggest-tech-companies-sold-to-private-equity-firm-for-more-than-2-billion.html|title=Consumer Cellular sells in deal pegged at $2.3B|date=28 October 2020}}</ref>

==Products==
Consumer Cellular sells no-contract monthly wireless plans with cutoff points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://lifehacker.com/why-i-love-this-mobile-carrier-for-old-people-1823732082|title=Why I Love This Mobile Carrier for Old People [Updated]|first=Nick|last=Douglas|website=Lifehacker|date=13 March 2018 }}</ref> It sells phones such as basic flip phones from Doro (of which the provider is the exclusive U.S. carrier), aimed toward seniors,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gadgetwise.blogs.nytimes.com/2009/11/03/more-tech-for-seniors/|title=More Tech for Older People|first=Eric A.|last=Taub|date=3 November 2009|publisher=}}</ref> as well as budget and flagship Android smartphones from Motorola and Samsung.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.consumercellular.com/blog/go-day-motorola-moto-e4-plus/|title=Go All Day and More with the Motorola Moto E4 Plus|date=19 October 2017 |publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.consumercellular.com/blog/experience-innovation-step-up-to-the-samsung-galaxy-note9/|title=Experience Innovation with the Samsung Galaxy Note9 Smartphone|date=10 September 2018 |publisher=}}</ref> In 2015, Consumer Cellular also began supporting the iPhone.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.consumercellular.com/blog/our-best-deal-ever-on-your-next-iphone/|title=Our best deal ever on your next iPhone.|date=30 March 2016 |publisher=}}</ref> The company expanded beyond cellphones in 2018 with the introduction of GrandPad,<ref>{{Cite news|date=2018-05-07|title=An iPad for 80-Year-Olds: Senior-Citizen Carrier Bets on Tablets|language=en|work=Bloomberg.com|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-07/an-ipad-for-80-year-olds-senior-citizen-carrier-bets-on-tablets|access-date=2020-09-09}}</ref> a simplified tablet designed for older users.

==Marketing and awards==
''[[Consumer Reports]]'' subscribers have rated Consumer Cellular highest in the magazine's annual review of cellphone service providers seven times.{{Citation needed|date=December 2025}} The magazine’s rankings are compiled from a survey of subscribers who grade carriers in eight different categories including value, voice and text quality, and customer support.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-01 |title=Best and Worst Phone Plan Providers |url=https://www.consumerreports.org/electronics-computers/cell-phones-services/best-and-worst-phone-plan-providers-a7549256764/ |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=Consumer Reports |language=en-US}}</ref>

Consumer Cellular has been ranked by [[J.D. Power]] as "#1 in Customer Service among Non-Contract Value Wireless Providers, 10 Times in a Row". The awards are based on the results of the J.D. Power 2016 V2 - 2020 V2 U.S. Wireless Non-Contract Customer Care Performance Studies and 2021 (V1) Wireless Customer Care Mobile Virtual Network Operator Performance Study, which focus on the experiences of wireless service customers who made a sales transaction with their current carrier.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jdpower.com/business/press-releases/2021-us-wireless-customer-care-studies-volume-1|title = 2021 U.S. Wireless Customer Care Studies - Volume 1}}</ref>

In June 2017, a consumer survey conducted by the customer experience firm Market Force Information named Consumer Cellular the favorite wireless cellphone carrier among non-contract providers for the second year in a row. Consumer Cellular came out on top for best value, best coverage, fewest dropped calls, easiest to change plan, and best flexibility, among others.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marketforce.com/2017-study-on-americas-favorite-wireless-carriers|title=New Market Force Study Finds T-Mobile and Consumer Cellular Are America's Favorite Wireless Carriers - Market Force Information, Inc.|website=www.marketforce.com}}</ref>

Readers polled by ''[[PC Magazine]]'' ranked Consumer Cellular as top mobile carrier in its annual "Consumer Recommended" list for 2018. The rankings were based on a company’s net promoter score, with Consumer Cellular’s score of 87 out of 100.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/365392/consumer-recommended-2018-the-tech-brands-you-love-most|title=Consumer Recommended 2018: The Tech Brands You Love Most|first=Eric|last=Griffith|date=December 12, 2018|website=PC Magazine}}</ref> Consumer Cellular has also been selected as "Favorite Wireless Carrier" by ''PC Magazine'' readers six years in a row in its "Reader’s Choice" survey.<ref>[https://www.pcmag.com/news/367381/buying-a-new-phone-these-are-the-brands-carriers-and-oses Buying a New Phone? These Are the Brands, Carriers, and OSes to Pick]</ref>

In 2024, Consumer Cellular entered a sponsorship deal with [[NASCAR Cup Series]] team [[RFK Racing]] to sponsor [[Brad Keselowski]] in multiple races during the [[2024 NASCAR Cup Series|2024 season]]. It has continued to sponsor Keselowski and [[Ryan Preece]] since then.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=January 24, 2024 |title=Consumer Cellular joins RFK Racing, will sponsor Brad Keselowski in multiple races |url=https://www.jayski.com/2024/01/24/consumer-cellular-joins-rfk-racing-will-sponsor-brad-keselowski-in-multiple-races/ |access-date=December 10, 2024 |website=[[Jayski's Silly Season Site]] |language=}}</ref>
